subject: HarborBank RFP: Support coverage, escalation flow & incident comms
messages:
From: Luke Brennan <luke.brennan@harborbank.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HarborBank Procurement <procurement@harborbank.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 12:12:00 -0400
Subject: HarborBank RFP: Support coverage, escalation flow & incident comms

Ben / Monica —

Thanks for taking on HarborBank's support appendix. Attached is the HRB support questionnaire (HB_RFP_TechQuestions.xlsx). We need written responses addressing our operational expectations by COB Monday. High level asks:

1) Provide your on-call/TAM coverage model (hours, handoffs, SLAs for P1/P2/P3).
2) Show the escalation path from TAM -> Support -> SRE/Eng (including SLA windows).
3) Incident communications: timeline templates we can use for security or availability incidents (initial notif, updates cadence, postmortem).
4) Any runbook/runplex you require from us (contacts, SSO, PagerDuty integration).
5) Provide references to SOC2 / pen test evidence delivery process.

We're planning procurement review Tuesday and need a succinct single-pager we can attach to the vendor comparison. If you can include an attachments list (SLA matrix + sample incident timeline) that would be ideal. CC'd Mike (ops) and procurement.

Appreciate it —
Luke
Senior IT Vendor Manager
HarborBank

Attachment: HB_RFP_TechQuestions.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Luke Brennan <luke.brennan@harborbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, HarborBank Procurement <procurement@harborbank.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 14:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: HarborBank RFP: Support coverage, escalation flow & incident comms

Luke —

Thanks for the clear list. We put together a one-page summary and a support matrix for HarborBank; attachments: redwood_harborbank_support_matrix.pdf and incident_runbook_appendixB.md. Key points up front:

- TAM coverage: Primary TAM (Monica Patel) 9x5 PST with overlap windows to cover US business hours; optional 24x7 coverage available as an add-on (recommended for production-critical deployments).
- Response SLAs (business hours / 24x7 add-on):
  * P1 (platform down / production blocking): 15 minute acknowledgement, 60 minute initial remediation update, continuous updates until mitigation.
  * P2 (degraded performance): 30 minute acknowledgement, 4 hour remediation plan.
  * P3 (general questions / config): 4 business hour acknowledgement, next-business-day resolution plan.
- Escalation path (summary): TAM -> Support L2 -> SRE/Model Ops L3 -> Engineering on-call -> Exec escalation. We include expected handoff windows and an example PagerDuty escalation policy in Appendix B.
- Incident comms cadence (template):
  * Initial notification: T+15m (acknowledgement + severity classification).
  * T+30/60m: Status update with scope & mitigation plan.
  * Hourly updates for active P1 until stability; then cadence reduces per runbook.
  * Post-incident RCA published within 5 business days; full postmortem within 10 business days for major incidents.
- Evidence & compliance: SOC2 Type II report available under NDA; pen-test summary and remediation logs are available via secure share once procurement executes the NDA.

Attachment notes: redwood_harborbank_support_matrix.pdf contains the matrix you can attach to your vendor comparison. The incident_runbook_appendixB.md details PagerDuty integration (service keys, recommended escalation chains), required IP allowlists for support access, and the minimum information we need from HarborBank to onboard (SAML SSO SAML metadata, primary on-call emails, emergency phone roster).

Next steps: Monica and I can join a 30-minute ops-review call Monday at 10am ET to walk through the matrix; if that works for procurement, we can handcarry the document into your Tuesday review.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0119

Attachments: redwood_harborbank_support_matrix.pdf (PDF), incident_runbook_appendixB.md (text)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Luke Brennan <luke.brennan@harborbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, HarborBank Procurement <procurement@harborbank.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:44:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: HarborBank RFP: Support coverage, escalation flow & incident comms

Luke / team —

Quick clarifications to Ben's summary (pulling from Appendix B):

1) 24x7 vs. 9x5: Our standard TAM + support model is 9x5 with on-call Support L2 available 24x7 for P1s when the optional 24x7 support add-on is purchased. The add-on includes a named follow-the-sun L2 engineer and a rotating L3 on-call.
2) Engineering escalation SLA: For P1 incidents where L3 work is required, we commit to engaging Engineering on-call within 30 minutes of L2 diagnosis (business or after-hours if add-on purchased). We maintain a documented escalation matrix with phone and PagerDuty escalation steps.
3) Communications templates: included in Appendix B are sample first-notice templates we use. Example: initial notice contains incident id, affected model/route, estimated user impact, current mitigation steps, and next update ETA.
4) RACI for postmortems: We deliver an interim incident summary within 48 hours (if requested) and a full RCA per contract timelines (default 10 business days). We can shorten those for enterprise contracts by agreement.

Security/compliance items:
- SOC2/pen test: we'll provision the SOC2 artifact via secure SFTP once the Mutual NDA is in place; we can also provide SOC2 controls mapping to your support and incident-handling questions.
- Access: we prefer ephemeral support sessions using customer-managed bastions and SSO-linked service accounts; details in Appendix B.

I'll join the Monday 10am ET call — suggest we have an ops contact from HarborBank (Mike or his designee) to verify primary escalation numbers and SSO contact.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Lead Technical Account Manager — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwoodinference.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 16:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: HarborBank RFP: Support coverage, escalation flow & incident comms

Lauren / Priyom —

Forwarding HarborBank's questionnaire and our proposed support matrix. Key commercial note: they listed 24x7 expectations in their RFP scoring rubric; we should propose the 24x7 add-on (named L2 + rotating L3) at the following recommended rate for enterprise (annual commitment): $75k/year for base 24x7 coverage + per-incident engineering uplift hours billed at our standard SOC rate. This keeps the base TAM pricing unchanged and preserves a clear upgrade path.

If procurement pushes for the SLA without add-on, we need explicit language limiting Engineering engagement during off-hours (response documented as 'best-effort' without add-on). Happy to be on the call Monday — please approve the commercial language below for the redlined SOW: "Optional 24x7 Support Add-on: includes named follow-the-sun L2 coverage and rotating L3 engineering on-call. P1 engagement SLA with Engineering: 30 minutes to engage support and 60 minutes for initial mitigation update when add-on purchased."

Ben

Luke
